Every climate shock is putting girls at risk: Study
item.description:
Climate disasters are driving greater risks of child marriage, teenage pregnancy, and violence for girls, according to a new global research by Plan International.

The study combines a large-scale analysis of health and climate data spanning more than 50 countries over three decades with a survey of 5,000 girls, in-depth interviews and focus group discussions with 139 girls, across Bangladesh, Kenya, Peru, Senegal, and Zimbabwe, says a press release.

The study found that climate disasters such as floods, droughts, cyclones, and extreme heat are destroying the health and education services girls depend on at the precise moment they need them most, with the consequences falling hardest on girls who already have the least.

Key findings of the report include:

One in 10 girls said they had personally experienced an unintended pregnancy following a climate-related event, while 33 per cent reported an increase in unintended pregnancies in their community.

One in 10 girls said they had personally married before the age of 18, and 36 per cent reported seeing more girls married or in a union before they turned 18 in their community following climate-related disasters.

More than a quarter (28 per cent) of girls said they had observed an increase in violence against women and girls following climate-related events.

Nine in 10 girls said climate-related events were placing serious pressure on their family's survival, health, and stability.

More than three-quarters (76 per cent) of girls said more girls and young women in their community were struggling to access at least one health service, rising to 84 per cent among those affected by drought.

Girls from minority communities were twice as likely to struggle to access services, nearly three times as likely to report an unintended pregnancy, and more than twice as likely to face pressure to marry young.

Behind many of these consequences lies a simple but devastating reality: climate shocks are pulling girls out of school. When education is disrupted, girls lose the single most protective factor in their lives, making them significantly more vulnerable to exploitation, violence, early marriage, and lost access to health services.

"For girls, the climate crisis is not a distant threat. It is already disrupting their education and increasing the risks they face when they cannot access health services. Only half of national climate plans mention girls’ or women’s health, and despite the escalating impact of climate shocks on the health systems and services girls rely on, just 0.5 per cent of multilateral climate finance supports health", said Reena Ghelani, Plan International CEO.

Girls reported increased risks of sexual exploitation in the aftermath of climate shocks, including being pressured into exchanging sex for money or basic necessities as protection systems and support networks break down.

Girls also reported heightened danger in emergency shelters, where cramped conditions and darkness left them exposed to harassment and sexual violence.

"When floods leave people completely destitute, families think about financial hardship and marry off girls at a very young age," said Shahina, 19, from Bangladesh. Participants in the study described girls becoming pregnant from as young as 12 and 13 in Peru, with girls in Zimbabwe noting pregnancy among girls still in primary and early secondary school.

Almost half of girls (49 per cent) noticed more pregnancy health or childbirth related complications, including miscarriages, in their community following a climate shock. Nearly one in four said access to healthcare during pregnancy and delivery care became harder to reach.

The research also identifies a form of climate harm that is almost entirely absent from disaster planning. Slow-onset drought destroys the household economies that keep girls out of marriage.

Across 52 countries and three decades, prolonged drought emerged as the hazard most consistently associated with rising rates of child marriage and early unions, as families lose harvests, livestock, and income over months and years until marrying a daughter becomes a survival strategy.

"My father has no livestock to sell and take me to college, that's how I accepted to be married off," said Galgalo, a 22-year-old participant from Kenya.

Because slow-onset drought rarely triggers an emergency response, this damage accumulates unseen. Girls whose schooling was disrupted were twice as likely to marry young or face an unintended pregnancy. A secondary analysis spanning over 50 countries across three decades confirmed that uninterrupted education is the single most consistent protective factor against early marriage and violence.

The findings highlight how climate-related disasters are exacerbating existing inequalities and vulnerabilities for girls, increasing risks to their health, safety, and wellbeing. This year, the El Niño weather pattern is intensifying weather extremes across the globe and predictions expect it to be the most powerful in decades.

In Peru, girls described how recurring El Niño floods disrupted access to health services, cut off transport routes, and increased pressure on already struggling families. With El Niño conditions projected to intensify further in the coming months, the window to act before these impacts deepen is narrowing.

With the world's attention soon to turn to COP31, where countries have an opportunity to negotiate international action on climate change Plan International is calling on governments and donors to act:

Keep schools open and free during climate shocks - education is the single most consistent protective factor across three decades of data, and girls whose schooling is disrupted are twice as likely to marry young or face an unintended pregnancy.

Allocate a defined share of climate adaptation finance to adolescent girls' health, including sexual and reproductive health services, contraception, and maternity care.

Include menstrual products, contraception, and protection services in every emergency response package, not as a later stage intervention

Reach the most marginalised girls. Girls from minority communities, those with disabilities, and those already displaced face the greatest barriers and receive the least support.

“We know what puts girls at risk, and we know what helps protect them. What is missing is not the evidence, but the urgency to act on it. Girls cannot continue to be treated as an afterthought in climate action. They must have a meaningful say in the decisions that shape their lives, and their rights and needs must be built into climate policy and financing from the outset”, said Reena Ghelani.

item.title: New Gini attack: Retired major general Mohiuddin secures bail
item.description:
A court has granted bail to former army officer Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury in a case filed over vandalism, looting and theft at the ‘New Gini Properties Limited’ housing project in the capital’s ECB Chattar area.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate (DMP) Aminul Islam Junaid granted him bail on Sunday after a hearing, on a Tk 2,000 bond. Tarek Rahman, sub-inspector of the DMP’s prosecution division, confirmed the matter to Prothom Alo on Monday.

He said the accused’s lawyers applied for bail after the remand ended on Sunday, and the court granted the application.

Planned in afternoon, attack at night, 2 gangs supplied men

According to court sources, Mohiuddin was produced before the court on Sunday after a three-day remand. On the same day, the case’s investigating officer and Detective Branch (DB) Inspector Jehad Hossain sought an order to keep him in jail.

At that point, Dhaka Bar Association General Secretary Mohammad Abul Kalam Khan sought bail on behalf of the accused. Following the hearing, the court granted bail until 28 October. No lawyer representing the prosecution was present at the hearing.

Mohiuddin was arrested from a house in Segunbagicha under Ramna police station on 30 September. The following day, 1 October, the court put him on three days’ remand.

Attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio: ‘Vandals entered New Gini Properties firing shots’

Around midnight on 26 September, a group of people armed with weapons attacked the housing project of New Gini Properties Limited in the capital’s ECB Chattar area. They fired around 50 shots indiscriminately and carried out an attack with machetes, knives and sticks.

At one point, the attackers entered the studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir and carried out extensive vandalism. They also looted various items from the studio. That night, Salman Muqtadir posted a video on social media showing his vandalised studio, sparking widespread discussion across the country.

In connection with the incident, project official Saiful Islam Bhuiyan filed a case with Cantonment police station. The case names 13 people as accused and includes another 150 to 200 unidentified people.

item.title: Deepto TV executive murder case: Court rejects plea to implicate minister Rabiul, 8 others
item.description:
A Dhaka court has rejected a petition seeking to implicate Road Transport Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam and eight others in the murder case of Deepto TV broadcast executive Tanzil Jahan Tamim in the capital’s Hatirjheel area.

The order was passed today, Monday, by Dhaka’s 13th Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Zahidul Islam after hearing the petition.

Court Bench Assistant Sohel Mia confirmed the matter, saying the nine individuals had earlier been discharged from the case. The complainant subsequently filed a revision petition challenging their discharge. The court has now rejected that petition, he said.

“The case will proceed against those who have been charge-sheeted,” Sohel Mia said.

Expressing dissatisfaction with the order, Abdul Alim, counsel for the complainant, said, “We are not satisfied with the order. We will move the High Court against it.”

Tamim was attacked at his home in the Mahanagar residential area of Hatirjheel on 10 October 2024. He was taken to hospital in critical condition, where physicians declared him dead. The following day, his father, Sultan Ahmed, filed a murder case with Hatirjheel police station.

The case named 16 people, including Mirza Abdul Latif, managing director of developer company Pleasant Properties; BNP Central Executive Committee member Sheikh Rabiul Alam; and Mohammad Mamun, deputy director of the Department of Narcotics Control. Eleven to 12 unidentified people were also named as accused.

On the day the case was filed, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) said at a press conference that Pleasant Properties, owned by Sheikh Rabiul Alam, had constructed a building on Tamim’s father’s land under an agreement. A dispute over the distribution of flats in the building had led to allegations that Mamun, a representative of the developer company, and several others beat Tamim to death.

Following its investigation, the Dhaka North unit of the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) submitted a charge sheet against 13 people and a delinquency report against a juvenile to the court on 10 December 2025. However, it recommended that nine people, including Rabiul Alam, be discharged for lack of “specific evidence” against them.

Dissatisfied with the recommendation, Tamim’s father Sultan Ahmed filed a no-objection petition with the court on 8 January.

On 3 March, Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Awlad Hossain Mohammad Junaid rejected the complainant’s petition and accepted the charge sheet in the case. He also discharged Rabiul Alam and the other eight from the case.

The 13 people against whom the charge sheet has been accepted are Pleasant Properties Ltd. Managing Director Mirza Abdul Latif, CEO Faizul Ahmed alias Suman, Mamunur Rashid Mamun, Korban Ali, SM Ibrahim Hossain, Badhan, Gazi Zakir Hossain, Russel, Monir Hossain, Shahraj Uddin, Amirul Islam alias Amir, Suman Mallik and Mahfuzar Rahman.

Those discharged from the case are Department of Narcotics Control Deputy Director Mohammad Mamun, Sheikh Rabiul Alam, Fazlur Rahman, Arian, Nasrin Akter, Russel, Mahfuzur Rahman, Mozammel Haque Kabir and Imam Hossain.

Sultan Ahmed filed the revision petition challenging their discharge.

item.title: Battery-powered rickshaw drivers block road in front of Press Club for an hour
item.description:
Battery-powered rickshaw drivers staged a protest and blocked the road in front of the National Press Club in the capital on Monday.

They initially gathered in Paltan at around 11:00 am before blocking the road in front of the National Press Club. The road remained closed to traffic for an hour.

According to eyewitnesses and police, the protesting drivers forced several passengers to get out of the rickshaws during the blockade, causing them inconvenience.

Police said the rickshaw drivers were protesting and blocked the road over several demands. The drivers demanded that battery-powered rickshaws charged using legal electricity connections not be disconnected. They also demanded that illegal connections not be disconnected.

Meanwhile, four rickshaw drivers were detained several days ago and sent to jail through executive magistrates. The protesting drivers also demanded their release.

Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of police in the Ramna division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), told Prothom Alo at noon that the rickshaw drivers had gathered there over several demands.

He further said police later went to the scene and brought the situation under control. Traffic is now moving normally.

item.title: No compromise on airport security: Civil aviation minister
item.description:
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat has said there will be no compromise whatsoever when it comes to airport security. He said the first few minutes are crucial if a fire or any other accident occurs at an airport, and the response time in emergencies must be reduced further.

The minister made the remarks today, Monday, after the ‘Airport Emergency Exercise (Fire)-2026’ drill at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka.

Rashiduzzaman Millat said fire safety and emergency response capabilities are key foundations for establishing a modern and secure aviation hub.

During a fire, immediate communication and coordination must be ensured among the Fire Service, airport authorities, operations and security teams, medical teams and other relevant agencies.

The minister said initiatives had been taken to sign memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with the relevant ministries and agencies to strengthen emergency response.

Referring to the fire at the airport’s import cargo complex last October, Rashiduzzaman Millat said the incident caused substantial damage and harmed the country’s image. Ensuring security is therefore the highest priority of the current government, he said.

The minister said that after taking office, the government had formed a National Civil Aviation Security Committee to strengthen security in the sector. An audit by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) will be conducted soon, he said, adding that measures had been taken to ensure compliance with issues that may be identified during the audit.

Rashiduzzaman Millat said no special security concessions would be given to VIPs or CIPs at the airport. Security protocols have been kept the same for everyone, he said, adding that everyone must follow those protocols to ensure airport security.

The minister said an initiative had been taken to install a comprehensive anti-drone system to prevent unauthorised drone flights.

He said the airport is a critical state facility and unauthorised drones had even been seen flying during the fire. A comprehensive anti-drone system will therefore be installed to prevent unauthorised drone flights in the airport area.

Rashiduzzaman Millat stressed the need to maintain an adequate number of security-related equipment at the airport, particularly scanners. He said it was the responsibility of everyone concerned to ensure passengers can travel safely, smoothly and comfortably.

The minister stressed the importance of implementing recommendations arising from the drill. He said emergency management capabilities must be further strengthened by implementing the recommendations that emerge from the post-drill assessment. Regular, realistic drills would improve the ability to respond quickly and effectively to emergencies, he said.

Punishment for Negligence

In response to questions from journalists after the drill, Rashiduzzaman Millat said the government had taken a strict stance against negligence of duty at the airport. He said the current government was a government of the people. Anyone who neglects their responsibilities would be punished, while those who perform their duties properly would be rewarded.

Asked about various allegations of passenger harassment and disorder at the airport recently, the minister said the authorities were taking steps to address the incidents that had occurred.

However, he said some misinformation was also being spread.

Asked about a woman’s allegation of harassment, Rashiduzzaman Millat said he had immediately looked into the matter. There was no truth to the incident as described, he said.

Addressing journalists, the minister urged them to inform the authorities if they came across genuine incidents. At the same time, he said, the truth must be reported and the spread of false information must be prevented.

In his closing remarks at the drill, Rashiduzzaman Millat said the government was committed to making the country’s civil aviation sector more modern, safe and up to international standards, with passenger safety and service receiving the highest priority. The collective efforts of all relevant institutions and agencies would continue towards achieving this goal.

Bangladesh Civil Aviation Authority (CAAB) Chairman Air Vice Marshal Md Mostofa Mahmood Siddiq and Dhaka-18 MP SM Jahangir Hossain also spoke at the event.

item.title: PM Tarique joins World Habitat Day discussion
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday joined a discussion marking World Habitat Day 2026, focusing on universal housing and sustainable urbanisation.
The program, organised by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, is being held at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka under the theme “Universal Housing, Sustainable Urbanisation.”
Before joining the program, the prime minister planted a Swarna Champa on the premises of the conference centre.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo, Housing and Public Works Minister Zakaria Taher Sumon, State Minister for Housing and Public Works Ahmad Sohel Manzur and ministry secretary Md Obaidur Rahman, among others, joined the programme.
A three-day housing fair has been organised at the lobby of the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre as part of the World Habitat Day observance.
A total of 157 stalls have been set up at the fair, featuring housing and construction sector products and services, banking services, Rajuk, the Department of Architecture, the Public Works Department and other agencies under the Ministry of Housing and Public Works.
The prime minister is expected to inaugurate the fair after the discussion program.
A seminar on planned urbanisation and sustainable housing will also be held at the conference centre at 2:30pm.
World Habitat Day is also being observed across all divisions and districts of the country through various programs, including publication of a souvenir, special discussions on television and radio, and displaying banners, posters and festoons at important locations.
Since 1986, World Habitat Day has been observed in Bangladesh and countries around the world.

item.title: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
item.description:
Three female journalists have accused Delhi Police personnel of sexual harassment while covering protests in the Indian capital against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, reports BBC.
The allegations were made on Saturday after police detained scores of protesters demanding Kumar’s resignation.
Delhi Police said the New Delhi district had received the complaints and transferred them to the Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial” inquiry.
Thousands of protesters gathered in Delhi and Mumbai on Sunday for a third consecutive day, demanding Kumar’s resignation over changes to voter rolls. The Election Commission says the revision aims to remove duplicate and ineligible entries, while opposition parties and protesters allege the process could disenfranchise eligible voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The BJP and Election Commission have rejected the allegations.
Videos circulating online showed protesters being detained and dragged away from the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.
The journalists’ allegations include inappropriate touching by police personnel. One journalist has also accused an assistant commissioner of police of sexually assaulting her while she was recording police action. The complaints are being investigated by the Crime Branch.
Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said women fear for their safety and that the Home Ministry must answer for the incident.
“Police dragged me by my hair,” Aahna Singh, an activist and student at Jawaharlal Nehru University, told Reuters during the protests. She accused police of “brutality.”
The Press Club of India has condemned the alleged treatment of journalists during the protests and demanded immediate action on the complaints against police personnel.
The organisation said it was “shocked and dismayed” by the reported treatment of journalists, adding that journalists must be allowed to work freely and document protests without fear.
The protesters say the voter-roll revision will benefit the BJP.
The Election Commission, however, says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries and update voter rolls to account for people who have died, left the country or registered at more than one address.
The revision, known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), has been controversial, with opposition parties accusing the Election Commission of manipulating voter rolls to favour the BJP. The BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the allegations.
The protests have included supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which began as an online satirical movement and has since become a youth-led political pressure group.
The CJP called for the latest protests following reports that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections to decisions and orders issued by Kumar.
The Election Commission has defended its decision-making process, saying differing views are part of the process and that decisions were taken unanimously.
The reported differences have further fuelled opposition demands for Kumar’s resignation.

item.title: Unplanned urbanization puts Dhaka at growing risk
item.description:
Dhaka is becoming increasingly difficult to live in as unplanned urbanization, rising population density, and inadequate civic infrastructure continue to put pressure on the capital.
The city lacks sufficient roads, open spaces, green areas, playgrounds and water bodies, while access to affordable housing remains a major challenge for low- and lower-middle-income households.
Urban planners warn that unless population density, building intensity and development are brought under effective control, Dhaka's liveability will continue to deteriorate.
The concerns come as Bangladesh observes World Habitat Day on Monday under the theme “Universal Housing, Sustainable Urbanization.”
The day is observed globally on the first Monday of October every year following a decision by the UN General Assembly in 1985. It has been observed since 1986 to raise awareness about housing, human settlements and sustainable urban development.
In Bangladesh, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works has arranged a discussion at the National Osmani Memorial Auditorium at 10am today to mark the occasion.
But experts say the reality of Dhaka's urban development remains far removed from the goal of sustainable and inclusive housing.
According to the Population and Housing Census 2022, Dhaka division has the country's highest population density, with 2,156 people living per square kilometre.
The enormous concentration of people in the capital and its surrounding areas has placed growing pressure on housing, roads, drainage, water supply, sanitation, waste management and other essential services.
Urban planners say simply constructing more high-rise buildings cannot solve Dhaka's housing crisis.
Housing must be planned alongside schools, hospitals, community centres, roads, parks, playgrounds, water bodies and other civic facilities, they say.
Adequate natural light and ventilation, green spaces and open areas must also be ensured within residential developments.
Instead, the rapid expansion of buildings and the drive to maximise land use have often taken precedence over broader urban planning considerations.
The housing crisis is particularly severe for low- and lower-middle-income residents.
While the private sector continues to develop high-end apartments and housing projects, affordable housing options for low-income households remain inadequate.
In this regard, Professor Dr Adil Muhammad Khan, executive director of the Institute for Planning and Development (IPD), said the constitutional commitment to ensure adequate housing has not translated into equal access to housing opportunities.
“Disparities in housing are increasing day by day,” he said.
According to him, government investment in housing and settlements for low- and lower-middle-income people in urban areas remains inadequate.
“Sustainable cities and human settlements cannot be built by leaving the housing sector solely to the profit-driven approach and strategies of the private sector,” he said.
He called for large-scale affordable housing projects for low-income groups, alongside measures to control Dhaka's population growth, manage density and strengthen development controls.
The Dhaka Detailed Area Plan (DAP), prepared to guide the capital's future development, was approved in August 2022.
The plan sought to control building intensity, housing density and the number of flats that could be constructed in different areas, with the broader objective of making Dhaka more liveable.
However, landowners and real estate developers strongly opposed several provisions of the plan.
Some amendments were introduced in September 2023 following their demands. But the changes failed to satisfy all stakeholders, prompting another initiative to revise the DAP.
Following the political change in 2024, the interim government formed a high-level advisory committee on the issue.
Based on recommendations from the committee, the DAP was revised for a second time, with a gazette notification issued in December 2025.
Urban planners have strongly criticised the repeated revisions, arguing that a long-term metropolitan development plan should not be repeatedly altered before its effectiveness can even be properly assessed.
Professor Adil said the success or failure of any urban plan ultimately depends on political commitment, proper enforcement, adequate financing, development control, the rule of law and impartial implementation in the public interest.
He said the 2022 DAP contained specific proposals addressing many of these issues.
“Yet within three years of its approval, the plan was amended twice under pressure from real estate interests, increasing floor area ratios (FAR), housing units and population density in various areas,” he said.
At the same time, he said, proposals for affordable housing, neighbourhood parks, playgrounds, primary schools and other civic facilities have remained largely unimplemented.
He argued that Dhaka's declining liveability was not caused by a lack of plans.
Rather, the failure to properly implement previous structure plans, master plans and DAPs has been a major reason behind the city's worsening conditions.
Professor Adil said the issue of population-density zoning had been compromised from the beginning.
According to him, the authorities gradually moved away from area-based height zoning proposed in the draft DAP towards an FAR-based approach, followed by increases in permissible FAR in different areas.
“This was a compromise at every stage,” he said.
He stressed that a liveable city requires not only population-density planning but also effective management of development intensity.
He also warned that amendments allowing greater construction intensity could restrict the flow of natural light and air into buildings, potentially creating further public health risks.
The concern is particularly important in a densely populated megacity where ventilation, open space and access to greenery are already limited.
The Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (Rajuk), however, maintains that the DAP remains essential for planned housing and urban development.
Ashraful Islam, chief urban planner of Rajuk and project director of the DAP, said the plan was prepared to transform Dhaka into a functional and liveable metropolitan city.
He said 58 areas have been identified under the DAP for affordable housing targeting low- and lower-middle-income households.
Under the proposed arrangements, low-income residents would have opportunities to own homes through affordable housing schemes and long-term instalment payments.
The revised DAP has been sent to the Planning Commission for approval, he said, adding that implementation would begin after approval.
Urban experts say Dhaka's fundamental problem is not a shortage of plans but weak implementation and inadequate development control.
Over the years, successive plans have been prepared to address congestion, housing, transport and environmental challenges. Yet implementation has frequently fallen behind the pace of urban expansion.
The result is a city where population and building density are rising while roads, parks, playgrounds, water bodies and other public amenities continue to shrink.
Experts argue that repeatedly changing planning regulations without ensuring basic civic infrastructure risks further worsening the imbalance between private development and public interest.
For Dhaka to remain liveable, they say, authorities must prioritise affordable housing, control population density, protect open spaces and water bodies, expand green areas and ensure schools, hospitals, roads and other essential services alongside residential development.
The challenge is therefore no longer simply to prepare another plan for Dhaka.

item.title: ACC case: Shajahan Khan, son shown arrested
item.description:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has filed a case against former shipping minister Shajahan Khan and his son, Ashibur Rahman Khan, over allegations of acquiring and possessing assets worth Tk9.89 crore disproportionate to their known sources of income.
A Dhaka court on Monday ordered that the two be shown arrested in the case.
Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Shahjahan Kabir passed the order following an application filed on September 7 by ACC Assistant Director Mahathir Muhammad Samir, who is investigating the case.
ACC lawyer Mohammad Khadimul Haque confirmed the matter.
While being taken from the court, Shajahan Khan told journalists: “You will see who speaks their mind.”
He also commented on the National Citizens Party (NCP) and Jamaat-e-Islami, saying: “By aligning with Jamaat-e-Islami, the NCP has effectively become Jamaat-e-Islami.”
During the hearing, defence lawyer Mizanur Rahman Badsha opposed the application to show the accused arrested.
He argued that the allegations and the filing of the case did not follow proper procedures.
The lawyer said nine bank accounts were mentioned in the case, three of which were in Shajahan Khan’s name, while the others were joint accounts. He also claimed that the value of the assets had been inflated in the allegations.
He said Ashib had paid taxes on the assets in accordance with the law.
The defence also sought bail, with the court fixing October 15 for a hearing on the petition.
According to the ACC case statement, movable and immovable assets worth Tk11.79 crore were found in Ashibur Rahman’s name.
The investigation found that his legitimate sources of income amounted to Tk1.90 crore.
The ACC said it found evidence of assets worth Tk9.89 crore that were disproportionate to his known sources of income.
The investigation report further alleged that Shajahan Khan, while serving as a member of parliament and minister, abused his position to facilitate the acquisition of the assets in his son’s name using funds obtained through dishonest means, both directly and indirectly.
ACC Deputy Director Kamlesh Mondal filed the case as the complainant on February 2, 2025.
The court has set November 25 for submission of the investigation report.

item.title: Appeal filed seeking to increase Inu's sentence for crimes against humanity
item.description:
An appeal has been filed seeking an increase in the sentence handed down to Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (Jasad) President Hasanul Haq Inu by the International Crimes Tribunal in a case involving crimes against humanity, including the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July-August mass uprising.
Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim confirmed the matter on Monday.
On June 30, the International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Inu to 10 years in prison and fined him Tk1 lakh.
The verdict was delivered by a tribunal bench led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, chairman of International Crimes Tribunal-2.
Eight charges were brought against Inu. The tribunal sentenced him to 10 years in prison on the third charge. For charges 6 and 7, he was sentenced to 10 years in prison on each count and ordered to pay Tk1 lakh in compensation for each, totalling Tk2 lakh.
However, the tribunal acquitted him of charges 1, 2, 4, 5 and 8.
Despite the separate sentences, the tribunal ordered that the sentences be served concurrently, meaning Inu will serve a total of 10 years in prison.
On May 14, after hearing arguments from both sides, the tribunal kept the case under Curia Advisari Vult (CAV), meaning the verdict was reserved for a later date.
Prosecutors Faruk Ahammad, Moinul Karim and Abdus Sobhan Tarafder, among others, represented the prosecution at the hearing. Senior lawyer Mansurul Haque Chowdhury represented Inu and concluded the defence arguments.
The defence presented its arguments over nine days, highlighting various legal issues in Inu's favour. It also argued that Inu was not a member of parliament during the July 2024 mass uprising.
Mansurul Haque said Inu had no involvement in the killing of the six people in Kushtia. Witnesses in the case also said he was not present in Kushtia when the killings took place.
The verdict was subsequently published on September 20 after being signed by the tribunal bench led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury.
On August 5, 2024, amid the July-August movement, gunfire was reported at several locations in Kushtia town, killing six people: worker Ashraful Islam, Suruj Ali Babu, students Abdullah Al Mustakin and Usama, businessman Bablu Faraji, and employee Yusuf Sheikh.
Several others were also injured in the violence.
A case was later filed against Inu at the International Crimes Tribunal in connection with the killings. Based on an investigation agency report, the prosecution subsequently submitted formal charges outlining eight allegations against him.

item.title: Rashed Khan: Kushtia BNP not involved in attack on Nasiruddin Patwary
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan has said BNP leaders and activists in Kushtia were not involved in the attack on National Citizens Party (NCP) leader Nasiruddin Patwary.
He made the remarks in a social media post on Sunday night.
Rashed Khan said Patwary had been in Kushtia since Saturday and visited various parts of the district. According to him, no BNP leader or activist, or member of any affiliated organisation, was involved in any altercation with Patwary.
He said Patwary later visited the shrine of Lalon Shah with NCP leaders and activists and spent considerable time with the devotees there.
“While they were leaving, an argument broke out between NCP members and some other individuals, leading to an unfortunate incident in which a vehicle was vandalised. BNP leaders and activists in Kushtia had no involvement in the incident,” Rashed Khan wrote.
He said he had spoken with local administration officials and BNP leaders about the matter, adding that none of them had been aware of Patwary’s visit to the Lalon Shah shrine.
Rashed Khan also questioned why Patwary had not informed the administration about his visit.
He said police arrived immediately after learning about the incident. However, according to his post, Patwary travelled a short distance under police escort before switching vehicles and leaving the area.
Rashed Khan contrasted this with an earlier incident in Jhenaidah, where Patwary went directly to a police station following an incident.
He questioned why Patwary had allegedly avoided police and left the area after the Kushtia incident, saying the circumstances raised “certain suspicions.”

item.title: Messi readies for final farewell in Argentina send-off
item.description:
Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions.
After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain's armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.
Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina's emerging generation.
The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima.
Messi also bows out as Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.
His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina's ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression.
"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
- Friends reunited -
Members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad -- the players who delivered the country's third star -- and their families will join Messi for Tuesday's farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world.
Veterans of that Doha triumph such as Angel Di Mar¡a, who retired from international football in 2024, will be there to witness the passing of the torch to a new generation charged with extending the Albiceleste's golden era.
Several of the newcomers, including Franco Mastantuono and Leonel Flores, were not even born when "La Pulga" ("The Flea") made his Argentina debut in 2005 for a team whose history had for so long been dominated by Diego Maradona.
"It's going to be an unforgettable day for everyone. Everyone wants to be at this match, and now it's just about enjoying it," Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said.
Argentina's new generation has already shown what it can do without its captain, although nobody is pretending replacing a man regarded by many as the greatest footballer in history will be straightforward.
"Collectively, we will try to fill the void left by Leo," said Scaloni, who is negotiating a contract extension after leaving his future unresolved following the World Cup defeat in July.
Scaloni, who mastered the art of building the right supporting cast around Messi, will also say goodbye on Tuesday to 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolas Otamendi.
Like Messi and Otamendi, midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up solely for the Benin game, raising the possibility that neither will represent Argentina again.
- New generation -
Those certain to be involved, at least from the bench, include other veterans of the 2022 World Cup who will be the standard-bearers for Argentina after Messi: defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez, and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.
Tenacious centre-back Romero is set to inherit the captain's armband, first worn by Messi at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Lautaro Martinez are next in the captaincy hierarchy.
They have already begun to rally around Messi's heirs, who showed their appetite for success in Argentina's first game since the World Cup final, against Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday.
Argentina swept the Bolivians aside 4-0, with young talents Nico Paz and Jose Manuel Lopez among the scorers.
They followed that victory with a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso at the Monumental on Saturday, with Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni scoring their first international goals.
While Argentina's future is beginning to take shape, one small but symbolically significant question remains: who inherits Messi's number 10 shirt?
"We won't give the number 10 to anyone until Leo's match takes place," Scaloni said. "After that, we'll see."

item.title: Battling Djokovic stuns top seed Zverev at China Open
item.description:
Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.
The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite.
He got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.
Boos filled the stadium soon afterwards when the umpire agreed to replay a point Djokovic had won, after Zverev complained about a flicker in the LED panels during play.
The German saw out the first set from there, but a valiant Djokovic roared back to seal the second with a cross-court winner to break serve and force a decider.
The 24-time Grand Slam champion faced 19 Zverev aces throughout the match but held steady on his own serve to go 5-4 ahead in the final set.
He then broke the world number two to take the set and the match, seemingly defying his recent physical difficulties with victory in a gruelling two hours and 34 minutes.
Djokovic will face Medvedev in the final four after the former world number one dispatched Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7/4), 6-3.
Poland's Hubert Hurkacz also advanced to the semi-finals after beating Karen Khachanov, and will play Australia's Alex de Minaur who survived a gruelling test to beat Andrey Rublev 1-6, 6-2, 6-3.
- Sabalenka swept out -
Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets in the third round, leaving the women's draw without its top two seeds.
Czech player Nikola Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.
"I focused on myself, to be calm," 34th-ranked Bartunkova said.
"She's a legend... so I'm really happy that I won the match," she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.
Bartunkova next faces Austria's Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.
A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.
Top seed Elena Rybakina -- who replaced Sabalenka as world number one weeks ago -- is also out, having lost to Alina Charaeva in the second round.
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva of Russia set up a fourth-round match with Ukraine's Daria Snigur, while Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova breezed past Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1.
Noskova next faces 28th-ranked Russian player Ekaterina Alexandrova.
Naomi Osaka, the 2019 champion, beat Sara Bejlek and will face either Karolina Muchova or Liudmila Samsonova, scheduled to play each other Sunday night.

item.title: Coach Jesus: Ronaldo can return to Portugal team if he wants
item.description:
Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the squad if he wishes, despite walking out on his team-mates, said national team coach Jorge Jesus on Sunday.
Jesus said Ronaldo can come back into the fold "if he wants to" after the team beat Norway without the veteran attacker to reach the Nations League quarter-finals.
The dispute began last week when Jesus left 41-year-old Ronaldo on the bench for Portugal's first win over Norway. Ronaldo subsequently walked out on the squad on Wednesday after learning he would not start against Denmark.
"For me, Cris, in the next call-up, if he's playing at Al-Nassr, he'll be a player who can be called up," Jesus told reporters, referring to Ronaldo's Saudi club side. "If he wants to, he'll return to the national team."
The coach said if Ronaldo wishes to speak to him before Portugal's next matches in November, that would happen.
"If he wants to, as we did before this call-up, we talked before the call-up, we can talk before the next call-up," continued Jesus. "But Cris is the one who's going to decide."
Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo is Portugal's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.
Jesus said he had told Ronaldo he needed him in the squad for his first games at the helm after replacing Roberto Martinez following the 2026 World Cup.
"Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants, he's the one who will decide how he wants it," said Jesus.
"That's how we talked, the two of us -- I said, 'I need you'. In my first call-up, I said, 'I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you'. And now I'm saying the same thing."
Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will "probably" be his final year in football.
The forward has been a fixture of the national team for more than two decades and has played at six World Cups.
In Ronaldo's absence Portugal became the first team to secure a place in the quarter-finals, with two group games still to play.
Ronaldo's long-time rival for the title of the world's best player, Lionel Messi, will play his final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires on Tuesday.

item.title: Ireland players wear black armbands, refuse handshakes with Israel in 1-1 draw
item.description:
Ireland players wore black armbands and bowed their heads during Israel's national anthem to protest Israel's actions in Gaza before the two teams drew 1-1 in a tense Nations League soccer match on Sunday.
Israeli players also wore black armbands to remember those killed in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. Israel captain Dor Peretz had “7.10” written on his armband.
Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher, who captained the team in place of Dara O'Shea, avoided shaking hands with Peretz before the match. O'Shea was excused from the squad to be with his wife for the birth of their child.
Kelleher followed the example of O'Shea, who had avoided shaking hands with Israel captain Manor Solomon before Ireland's 3-0 victory in their first meeting in Debrecen, Hungary, last week. Ireland scored all three goals in the first half of that match.
Solomon was named among the substitutes for Sunday's game in Backa Topola, Serbia. Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi returned to the squad after serving a suspension for his red card following a goal celebration during a 3-1 defeat to Austria on September 25, but did not feature in the match.
Irish forward Finn Azaz, whose mother has Israeli heritage, also remained among the substitutes.
Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead from the penalty spot in the 39th minute after Peretz fouled Jimmy Dunne. Tensions rose on the touchline as players headed into the dressing rooms at half-time.
Peretz raised the back of his jersey above his neck before the second half, apparently highlighting the Israeli flag on it. He then equalised from close range just two minutes after the restart.
Israel came close to taking the lead in the second half, with substitute Omri Gandelman and Oscar Gloukh both hitting the right post. Spanish referee Juan Martínez Munuera had to remain alert as tensions flared following several strong challenges.
The match was originally scheduled to take place in Dublin, but the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) moved it to a neutral venue in June for “operational reasons” following widespread calls to boycott the fixture. The FAI also announced that the match would be played without spectators.
The decision followed an FAI motion in November last year calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.
Pressure on Irish players
Irish players faced growing pressure at home to boycott the two matches against Israel, reflecting strong public support for Palestinians. The pressure was particularly intense ahead of the first match.
“I felt that pressure growing day by day and it's getting almost to a breaking limit now,” Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said before the first game.
Ultimately, only reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from both matches. In a statement, he said it was his “personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong.”
More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to play the two fixtures.
Before the team travelled to Hungary, protesters gathered outside their Dublin hotel, urging the players to boycott the matches. The SIPTU trade union also displayed a large poster beside the River Liffey in central Dublin, calling on the players to “Go with your conscience!” and “Don't play with genocide,” alongside an image of a blood-splattered football.
Former Ireland coach Brian Kerr said the FAI had “lost the respect of the Irish people” by proceeding with the matches.
However, the FAI resisted the calls, arguing that Ireland could face severe sanctions from UEFA if the team refused to play. Ireland is scheduled to co-host the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.
Tense build-up to match
The fixtures have been preceded by several protests and confrontations.
During Ireland's 2-2 draw with Austria on Thursday, protesters threw tennis balls bearing Palestinian flags onto the pitch. A man carrying a Palestinian flag later attempted to run onto the field.
Tensions also surfaced at Saturday's pre-match news conference when an Israeli journalist alleged that Irish players had called Israeli players “monkeys” during the first match. Ireland's communications officer, Kieran Crowley, immediately rejected the allegation as “a lie” and ended the news conference.
The Irish players had agreed to proceed with the fixtures only after lengthy discussions in Debrecen before the first match. Both a news conference and a training session were delayed for hours as the squad considered its options. Reports said the players voted 14-8 in favour of playing after Bazunu withdrew that morning.
Ireland's national broadcaster RTÉ provided limited coverage of both matches to fulfil its contractual obligations. It omitted studio presentations, commentary on the international feed and post-match analysis. The broadcaster also said it would not accept advertising or sponsorship associated with either game.
RTÉ recently announced that Ireland would boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second consecutive year because of Israel's participation.

item.title: Portugal move into Nations League knockout stage, Germany held
item.description:
Portugal became the first team to reach the quarter-finals of the Nations League when they beat Norway 2-1 on Sunday, but Jurgen Klopp's Germany were frustrated by Greece.
The Portuguese showed they did not need Cristiano Ronaldo, who walked out of the camp on Wednesday when coach Jorge Jesus relegated him to the bench.
Goncalo Ramos secured victory in the 86th minute after Joao Cancelo's powerful finish had levelled Kristoffer Ajer's stunning opener from outside the penalty area for World Cup quarter-finalists Norway.
After the game, Jesus said he was prepared to allow 41-year-old Ronaldo to return to the national team -- but that it would have to be the player's decision.
"If he wants to, he'll return to the national team... we can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who's going to decide," Jesus told reporters.
Jurgen Klopp's Germany failed to break down a resolute Greek side in a goalless stalemate in Thessaloniki.
Germany had the ball in the net through Eintracht Frankfurt forward Jonathan Burkardt in the first half but his effort was disallowed.
Klopp's record as new German boss now reads: lost one, won one, drawn one.
The Netherlands beat Serbia 2-1 thanks to Joshua Zirkzee's winner to move top of their Nations League group.
The Manchester United forward was a second-half substitute in Eindhoven and applied the decisive touch with a tap-in from Tijjani Reijnders' cross.
The match also marked Virgil van Dijk's 100th international appearance.
New Netherlands coach Xavi is unbeaten after four games, with two wins and two draws.
Israel's players wore black armbands in their 1-1 draw against Ireland to commemorate the victims of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack, after Irish players had worn them in the previous match in Hungary to protest the war in Gaza.
The simple black armbands worn by the Israelis were inscribed with the numbers "7.10" to mark the date of the attack.
Just as in last week's first match which Ireland won 3-0, the Irish players again bowed their heads during the Israeli anthem and the teams refused to shake hands before the match in the small Serbian town of Backa Topola.
The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had refused to host Israel on Irish soil for security reasons, following boycott calls.
On Sunday, Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead from the penalty spot after 39 minutes after Dor Peretz fouled Jimmy Dunne.
But Peretz stabbed in an equaliser two minutes after half-time, sending in from close range after a shot deflected off Ireland defender Liam Scales and into his path.
The result complicates Ireland's qualification task as they now lie third in Group 3 of League B behind Austria and Kosovo. Israel are bottom with two points.
Wales lost again, as Rasmus Hojlund slotted in a 75th minute penalty to earn Denmark a 1-0 win in Cardiff.
Welsh goalkeeper Danny Ward had kept the Danes at bay with a string of saves but he conceded the penalty when he fouled Denmark midfielder Gustav Isaksen.

item.title: Shopping malls, markets can stay open until 10pm for Durga Puja
item.description:
The government has extended the operating hours of shopping malls, markets and stores across Bangladesh ahead of Durga Puja 2026, allowing them to remain open from 11am to 10pm until October 22.
The directive was issued on Monday, October 5, 2026, through an office order signed by Sonia Binte Tabib, deputy secretary of the Electricity Division’s Coordination-2 branch under the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources.
According to the order, shopping malls, markets and stores can remain open daily from 11am to 10pm until October 22.
From October 23, the previous schedule of 11am to 8pm will resume and remain in effect.
Copies of the order have been sent to the mayors or administrators of all city corporations, divisional commissioners, deputy commissioners and other relevant offices for necessary action.

item.title: Man shot dead in Khulna 50 days after son’s murder
item.description:
A man was shot dead in Khulna’s Rupsa upazila on Monday evening, 50 days after his son was shot and hacked to death in the same area.
The deceased was identified as Aktar Dhali, 64, of Durjani Mahal village under Aichgati union. The incident occurred around 6:45pm, when Aktar was sitting on a bench beside the road in front of his house.
Family members said they suddenly heard gunshots and came outside to find Aktar lying beside the bench. Unidentified assailants had shot him before fleeing the scene.
Doctors at Khulna Medical College Hospital declared him dead after he was taken there.
Murad Hossain, an emergency department staff member at Khulna Medical College Hospital, said Aktar had been shot in his right shoulder. He may also have sustained injuries from shotgun pellets.
Rupsa Police Station Officer-in-Charge Anwar Zahid said: “Police have been sent to the place where Aktar Dhali was shot. We are investigating who carried out the incident and why. The body is being processed for autopsy.”
He said: “Police have started investigating to identify and arrest those involved in the killing. We will also examine whether there is any connection between the 2 killings.”
Aktar’s son Joy Dhali, 27, was shot and hacked to death in the same area on August 15.
Police said a group of 4-5 people attacked Joy in front of Durjani Mahal in the Shaheed Mor area of Rupsa around 8:30pm that day. The helmeted assailants arrived on motorcycles and hacked him, killing him at the scene before fleeing on motorcycles.
The killing of Aktar triggered panic among local residents, while senior police officials visited the scene after receiving the news.
The body is being processed for autopsy, and police are investigating the killing and the possible connection between the 2 incidents.
